facts.text: I asked which functions are common to ERC-721 and which are custom.

I listed a set of contract functions by 4-byte selectors, including buyAlbum(bytes32[]), buySong(bytes32[]), publicMint(), destroyPublic(uint256,uint256), claimAlbum(uint256,uint256), tokenURI(uint256), setImportantURIs(string,string), reclaimERC20Token(address), reclaimERC721(address,uint256), setStartTimes(uint256,uint256,uint256,uint256), setMerkleRoot(bytes32,bytes32), setArtistWallet(address), setNFTContract(address), setRoyalty(address,uint96), setQuorum(uint256), setPricePerToken(uint256,uint256), setSplitsWallet(address), withdrawToSplits(), _isContract(address), _startTokenId(), supportsInterface(bytes4), isProofValid(address,uint256,bytes32[]), and isProofValid2(address,uint256,bytes32[]).

I described contract variables including baseURI, imageURL, contractURI, root, root2, ablumSaleStartTime, songSaleStartTime, publicStartTime, destroyExperienceStartTime, albumPrice, songPrice, belongsToAlbum, MAX_SUPPLY, quorum, songCounter, tokenTypesMap, destoryExperinceVotes, isRestricted, splitsWallet, nftContract, and artistWallet.
I asked to put all of these functions in a table with a column indicating whether each function is standard or custom.
I asked why tokenURI is considered custom and whether tokenURI is part of a standard.
I asked for a brief description of what each function does in a separate column, to the extent that the assistant knows.
